blocks.title: Wireless and Mobile Security exam shortcuts
items: The device belongs to the user, creating privacy and management challenges.
Example: A personal phone accesses company email.
Company owns device but permits personal use → COPE
The organization retains stronger control while allowing limited personal use.
Example: A company-issued phone permits personal apps.
User chooses from approved models → CYOD
Choice is limited to a corporate-approved list.
Example: Employees select one of three supported phones.
Need to plan AP placement → SITE SURVEY
Evaluate coverage and interference before installation.
Example: Measure signal throughout an office before mounting access points.
Need visual coverage/dead-zone view → HEAT MAP
A heat map shows signal strength across the physical area.
Example: Weak coverage appears in a conference-room corner.
Need centralized mobile policy/remote wipe → MDM
MDM enforces controls across managed mobile devices.
Example: A lost phone is remotely wiped.
blocks.example: Focus on what the resource needs: baseline consistency, hardening, secure access, isolation, authentication, or monitoring.

questions.q: Before installing access points, engineers measure interference and coverage across the building. Which technique is this?
questions.explanation: A site survey evaluates the environment before wireless installation.

questions.q: A color-coded diagram shows strong and weak Wi-Fi signal areas throughout an office. What is this?
questions.explanation: A heat map visualizes wireless coverage and signal strength.

questions.q: A lost company phone must be remotely wiped and have screen-lock policy enforced centrally. Which solution is best?
questions.explanation: MDM centrally manages mobile-device policy and remote actions.

questions.q: An employee uses a personally owned phone to access company email. Which deployment model is this?
questions.explanation: BYOD means the user owns the device.

questions.q: The company owns the phone but permits limited personal apps. Which deployment model is this?
Employees may choose one of three company-approved phones. Which model is this?
questions.explanation: CYOD lets users choose from an approved device list.
